clue.text: See 1 down
Given suggestion to do manual work, I collapse or die, first to suffer really terrible death — fracas on a foreign street

definitions.text: Given suggestion to do manual work

indicators.note: on says the word for fracas is placed after the pieces before it

parts.note: to collapse is to fall down
'or else' — else stands in for or, offering the alternative
to die, of a machine or a plant, is to stop working or give out

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of each of the two words that follow it
terrible says the letters of death are wrecked and reassembled

parts.note: ein is German for a, so a foreign word for the article
ructions are a noisy fracas or uproar

explanation.surface: A gloomy, rambling account of someone told to do manual labour who would rather collapse and die, ending with a brawl abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles DEATH to EADTH, read with R from 'first to ... really' to give READ THE. 'Manual' is not handwork but a booklet of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock advice to consult the manual when everything has gone wrong, so it is a suggestion to make the handbook do its job.

clue.text: Ship, rather infested with cockroach, cleaned out

indicators.note: infested with says the word for rather has something living inside it

parts.note: 'I'd rather' and 'I'd sooner' mean the same, so rather gives sooner

indicators.note: cleaned out empties the word cockroach, leaving only its two end letters

explanation.surface: A vessel overrun with cockroaches has been fumigated and scrubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts, fore-and-aft rigged.

clue.text: Programmed factory worker to steal books

parts.note: to steal is to rob
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A worker on the factory floor has been told to pinch some books.
explanation.definitionFit: Automated arms on assembly lines are machines that follow a set program in place of human labour.

clue.text: Hardbacks from Sweden in accurate translation

indicators.note: in says the letter for Sweden is placed within the rearranged word
a translation renders the word accurate into a new form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Hardback books from a Swedish publisher, faithfully translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardbacks' looks like books, but it means creatures with hard shells; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and shrimps form a class of animals with tough outer shells, playfully called hard backs.

clue.text: I must have bits to eat

definitions.note: I is the chemical symbol of this element

parts.note: binary digits, bits, are 1 and 0, which look like the letters I and O
to eat a meal is to dine

explanation.surface: Someone insists they must have a few snacks to munch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the chemical symbol; 'bits' means binary digits, not morsels.
explanation.definitionFit: The halogen element with atomic number 53 has the chemical symbol I.

clue.text: Scar is sort of orange

definitions.meaning: the belly button is the scar left where the umbilical cord was cut
a seedless orange with a small belly-button-like mark at one end

explanation.surface: A scar described as orange-coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button is a healed scar from birth, and the seedless orange is named for its belly-button-like pit.

clue.text: Wears shoes?

parts.note: read as a question it is someone having shoes on; the other sense of wear is to damage footwear by scraping

explanation.surface: Is someone putting on footwear?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue turns on two senses of 'wear': having shoes on, and scraping them so the surface is marked.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape leather so it gets marked and worn is exactly what damage to footwear by dragging the feet does.

clue.text: Period in which I would always support father

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support is to sit below, so the pieces for I would and always come under the one for father

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
I'd is the contraction of I would
ay or aye is an old word for always, as in 'for ay'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a time when they would always back up their dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday is a span of time, one named day of the week.

clue.text: Argue about pound coins

indicators.note: about says the word for coins goes around the abbreviation for pound

parts.note: coins are cash
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Two people quarrelling over a pound's worth of change.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree fiercely or conflict, as opinions do, is a synonym for quarrelling.

clue.text: Restricted by court, easily clear

definitions.meaning: in English law a person can be ordered by a court to keep the peace on pain of forfeit

explanation.surface: Someone under a court order who nevertheless gets off easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal sense is a court order to keep the peace; the athletic sense is jumping lightly across an obstacle.

clue.text: Quarrel following strike call

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
'all out!' is the union's call to its members to strike

explanation.surface: A dispute arises after a union calls for industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who stop being friends after an argument are said to have had a row.

clue.text: Caught up with Dynasty and got ahead

parts.note: the Tang were a Chinese dynasty, 618 to 907
to have got ahead of the others is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone who has been following the TV soap Dynasty finally pulls ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught up in something means being snarled or entangled in it.

clue.text: Money bet on gorilla

parts.note: silver is coin money
to bet on a horse is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone stakes cash on a gorilla, as if it were in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult male gorilla develops a saddle of grey hair, giving him this name.

clue.text: At work, my partner may give me a lift

definitions.text: At work, my partner may give me a lift

parts.words: At work, my partner may give me a lift
parts.note: sounds like a colleague offering a ride, but a dancer's partner raises her overhead on stage

explanation.surface: A commuter mentions that a colleague sometimes drives them to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical dance the male partner raises the female dancer in lifts during a pas de deux.

clue.text: Question imbibing English dairy product

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the question word takes in the letter

parts.note: why is a question word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an English dairy product is worth drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheesemaking is a by-product of the dairy.

clue.text: Try a couple of old drawers at first — trunks hold me in

parts.note: a judge hears a case when trying it
a couple of things is two of them

indicators.note: at first takes the initial letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone tries on old underwear, the trunks holding them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' and 'trunks' look like underwear; the trunks are those of trees, and the definition speaks as the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The dense, dead central wood of a tree trunk is held at the core, inside the living sapwood.

clue.text: Vault across ship is our aim, ridiculously

indicators.note: across says the rearranged letters lie on both sides of the abbreviation for ship
ridiculously says the letters of our aim are jumbled into a silly order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone declares that their target is to vault right across a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a leap but is a burial chamber; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A charnel house or bone vault is a place where the bones of the dead are stored.

clue.text: Works in bed turning ends of socks

indicators.note: turning ends of says the two letters at the end of the word for socks swap places, so the last one steps back

parts.note: hose are stockings or socks

explanation.surface: Someone in bed busies themselves turning the toes of their socks, as in darning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a garden flower bed, not a bed for sleeping in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener breaks up soil and weeds a flower bed with a long-handled tool; the verb means to work the earth.

clue.text: Poet in hot competition to secure love

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the pieces for hot and competition hold the letter for love

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a race is a competition
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet in a fierce contest tries to win someone's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintus Horatius Flaccus was a Roman lyric poet of the Augustan age, known for his Odes.

clue.text: Has bath just before bed for a fresh start

parts.note: someone having a bath cleans themselves
the time just before bed is late in the evening

explanation.surface: Taking a bath right before going to sleep is a way to begin anew.
explanation.definitionFit: A record wiped free of past mistakes lets someone begin again, an idiom from wiping a writing tablet.

clue.text: Very eager to start next page after turning

indicators.note: to start takes only the opening letter of eager

parts.note: the verso is the left-hand page, the one you see after turning a leaf

explanation.surface: A keen reader can't wait to turn over to the next page.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase means extremely, as in 'thanks awfully much'.

clue.text: Guide round home, a turn up for the book

indicators.note: a turn up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top
round says the word for guide goes around the word for home

parts.note: to guide is to lead
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A guide showing someone around the house finds a surprising volume, 'a turn-up for the books' being a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the idiom 'a turn-up for the books', meaning a surprise; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament contains a prophetic book named after the man thrown into the lions' den.

clue.text: Get pumped up about female behind

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to be behind schedule is to be late

explanation.surface: Someone gets excited about a woman's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate again, as a tyre or a ball is filled with air once more, or an economy stimulated.

clue.text: See 1
See 1 down
In second city, head to the bottom area steps

indicators.note: head to the bottom says the first letter moves to the end, the bottom of a down entry

parts.note: Brum is Birmingham, often called Britain's second city

explanation.surface: In Birmingham, someone makes for the lower part of a set of stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Brum is the nickname for Birmingham, an English city in the Midlands. 'steps' means dance steps; 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance is a set pattern of steps performed to its distinctive rhythm.

clue.text: Twitch is part of villain's complaint

indicators.note: part of says the pieces for twitch and is become part of the word for villain, inside it

parts.note: crim is slang for a criminal or villain
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A villain's nervous twitch is one of the things wrong with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like an illness, matching 'twitch', but it means finding fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding fault with someone and voicing disapproval is making a complaint about them.

clue.text: One may be clapped into these clubs

definitions.text: One may be clapped into these
definitions.meaning: chains or fetters a prisoner is clapped into

explanation.surface: A prisoner clapped in irons, set beside golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackles of metal hold a prisoner, and numbered golf clubs with angled metal heads share the name.

clue.text: It's obvious I don't think casual dreams need interpretation

indicators.note: dreams that need interpretation must be decoded, so the letters of casual dreams are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismisses the idea that casual dreams need to be analysed, Freud-style.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic simile means not at all clear, a sarcastic way of saying something is obscure.
